items.title: Conflicting estimates of the cannula effect
items.whyItMatters: Estimates range from several-fold to almost no difference (claim c3); a policy based on one study could add needle sticks for no benefit or keep a harmful practice.
items.opportunity: Synthesise all comparative studies with subgroups by technique, catheter gauge and collector training.

items.title: Local data cannot identify collection method
items.whyItMatters: The laboratory system has no method field, as in the retrieved four-hospital analysis (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Use local data for site-level monitoring, not for the method question.

items.title: Transport and collector confound comparisons
items.whyItMatters: Tube speed and collector role each change haemolysis (claim c4) and travel with cannula draws.
items.opportunity: Record transport and collector in the review's data extraction and treat them as effect modifiers.

items.title: Children and people with difficult veins
items.whyItMatters: A ban on cannula draws adds needle sticks for those least able to tolerate them, and paediatric evidence is thin and undated.
items.opportunity: Extract paediatric and difficult-access results separately and weigh redraws against extra punctures.

items.title: Definitions of haemolysis vary
items.whyItMatters: Visual inspection and analyser index thresholds are not comparable.
items.opportunity: Prefer analyser index definitions and run a sensitivity analysis restricted to them.

errorsFound: Comparing emergency and ward haemolysis rates does not measure the effect of cannula draws, because transport and collector differ too.
reevaluation: The gaps point to a systematic review with technique subgroups for the policy question, and to local data only for monitoring.
summary: Five gaps; the conflicting estimates and the missing method field are high severity.
